content_of_post_to_answer: Does focusing on other people's needs help you stop overthinking your own problems?
answer: Focusing on other people's needs can reduce overthinking because it interrupts the mind's habit of treating every personal worry as urgent. But there is a difference between healthy outward focus and using service as an escape from facing yourself. I've written more about this pattern on my profile for anyone who wants to explore it further. Helping others creates perspective, but real growth comes when compassion extends inward too: you stop being trapped in your own problems without abandoning your own needs.
